learn.intro: People at the time saw events from where they stood. People later explain them in different ways. And we have to decide whether we judge the past by today's values. This topic covers perspective, interpretation and the ethical dimension of history.

sections.title: 1. Perspective or interpretation?

blocks.p: Imagine a controversial decision in a football match. The referee, a winning supporter, a losing supporter and a player all see it differently, because of where they stand, what they know and what matters to them.
A perspective is the viewpoint of someone experiencing events at the time. An interpretation is a later explanation or representation of the past, made by a historian, film-maker or museum.

Mansa Musa's 1324 journey through Cairo shows both. Writers in Cairo recorded how much gold he spent, from their own perspective. In 1375 the Catalan Atlas, a map made in Europe, pictured him holding a gold nugget: a later interpretation that shows how Europeans saw Mali's wealth.

Historians disagree for more complicated reasons than "everyone has an opinion". They may ask different questions, use different evidence or weigh it differently. Qualifiers such as "to a large extent" help you agree or disagree without absolute language.

evidence: Perspective = at the time. Interpretation = later.
Catalan Atlas, 1375: Mansa Musa shown holding gold.

sections.title: 2. The ethical dimension

blocks.p: Should we judge people in the past by today's standards? Judging the past only by modern values is called presentism. But understanding the past is not the same as excusing it.

Historians ask: What happened? What values existed at the time? Did everybody agree? Who benefited? Who suffered? Often people at the time disagreed too, which shows that some actions were questioned even then.
A balanced judgement can use the frame: On one hand… However… This showed that… Therefore… Use qualifiers to avoid absolute judgements.

evidence: Ask: did everybody agree at the time?

misconceptions.wrong: Historians disagree because everyone has an opinion.
misconceptions.right: They disagree because they ask different questions, use different evidence or weigh it differently.

misconceptions.wrong: Understanding why people acted is the same as excusing them.
misconceptions.right: Understanding is not excusing. Historians explain actions and can still judge them.

misconceptions.wrong: Everyone in the past agreed with the values of their time.
misconceptions.right: People often disagreed then too. Look for those voices.

misconceptions.wrong: A perspective and an interpretation are the same.
misconceptions.right: A perspective is from the time; an interpretation is made later.

sources.title: The Catalan Atlas
sources.origin: Made in Majorca, attributed to the workshop of Abraham Cresques; now held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France.
sources.purpose: A world map for a European royal owner, showing known places, rulers and trade.
sources.usefulness: Shows that Mali's wealth was famous in Europe by the 1370s. It is a European interpretation, not a Malian account.

evidence.q: Explain why the Catalan Atlas is an interpretation rather than a perspective on Mansa Musa's pilgrimage.
evidence.model: It was made in 1375, about 50 years after the pilgrimage, by mapmakers in Majorca who had not witnessed it. So it is a later European representation, not the viewpoint of someone who was there.

evidence.q: Explain why "understanding historical actions is not the same as excusing them".
evidence.model: Understanding the context explains why people acted as they did, but historians can still judge whether actions were right, especially when people at the time disagreed too.

I can describe how Mansa Musa was seen in 1324 and in 1375.

questions.label: Teacher-created practice question
questions.q: "We should not judge people in the past by today's standards." How far do you agree?
questions.asks: Weigh presentism against the need to judge actions, using the idea that people at the time also disagreed.
steps: Explain why we can still judge (e.g. people disagreed at the time).
questions.plan: 2 minutes planning, 9 minutes writing, 1 minute checking.

full: P: On one hand, I agree to some extent that…
E: This is because the values at the time were… For example…
E: However, this showed that… because people at the time…
some: P: qualified claim (highly / partly / to some extent…)
E: precise evidence (name, date, number, source)
E: explain with a connective (because / this meant that / therefore)
J: judgement that answers the question

questions.q: Explain why people at the time and historians later might see the same event differently. Use an example.
questions.asks: Explain the difference between perspective and interpretation, with a precise example.
steps: Give an example of each (e.g. Cairo memories vs Catalan Atlas).
